Good morning and welcome to the regional commercial convention. A few practical points before the first session. Coffee is on the second floor, not on this one, and the coffee breaks are twenty minutes, which is shorter than usual because the programme is full. If you have never been to one of our regional events before, there are about ninety of us here, from four countries, and the working language is English for everything except the corridor. Your name badge has a coloured line at the bottom. Blue means commercial, green means operations, orange means you are a guest. Use it. It is the fastest icebreaker in the building.

I have been coming to these events for eleven years and I have learned exactly one thing that matters, so I will give it to you now. Do not try to meet everybody. In twenty minutes you can have one real conversation or six terrible ones, and the six will give you nothing. Find one person you have never spoken to, ask them something you actually want to know, and stay there. If they are interesting, say so, and ask for their email before you walk away. That is it. I have never once regretted a conversation I stayed in, and I have forgotten every single person I met for ninety seconds.

Andres introduces himself and says he has seen her name on the regional list but has never met her. Rosa says which office she works in and asks whether he has been to this convention before. Andres answers that he has attended it three times and explains what he has learned about the coffee breaks. Rosa asks whether he has already met the new regional director, and Andres says he has not met him yet. Andres suggests a next step, and Rosa agrees to send him something after the convention.
